title: Operator prefetch safety and obsolescence playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary
This playbook defines operator procedures, alerts, and governance for the lifecycle and safe retirement (obsolescence) of prefetch hints and related cache-prefetch artifacts in the Redwood runtime. It is oriented to platform operators, runtime engineers, and SREs who manage LLM KV/prefix caches and operator-side hint layers. The goal is to keep prefetch behavior safe for customer SLOs while preventing hint accumulation and stale behaviors across model/format changes.

Why this exists
- Prefetch hints reduce latency/cost but can become harmful when stale, mis-scoped or when models change.
- We need standard operator checks, alerting, and a retirement process so that hints do not degrade availability or violate SLAs.
- This playbook complements the runtime prefetch heuristics and the feature-flag rollout DSL.

Scope and non‑scope
- Includes: hint configuration schema versions, operator safety checks, alert thresholds, rollback and retirement procedures, telemetry required, ownership.
- Excludes: application-level prompt design and third-party tenant hint content policies (owned by customer success).

Key concepts and definitions
- Prefetch hint: a metadata object used by the runtime to proactively populate KV/prefix caches for a tenant/model/route.
- Hint TTL: wall-clock lifetime after which runtime will stop using an unpaid-for hint variant.
- Hint versioning: schema revision label (e.g., v1, v2) embedded in the hint body.
- Hint obsolescence window: operator-specified period between deprecation announcement and forced prune.

Owner and responsibilities
- Primary owner: eng-platform/runtime-team (oncall: runtime-sre rotation).
- Policy owner: product-engineering for new hint schema and semantics.
- Operator responsibilities: monitor hint-induced SLO impact, run synthetic validation when enabling new hint versions, coordinate deprecation with product and customer-success.

SLOs and alert thresholds (concrete)
- Latency SLOs: 99th-percentile p99 <= 2200ms for generation requests with prefetch-enabled routes.
- Error SLO: Error rate <= 0.3% measured per region per 5m window.
- Safety alert triggers (high-priority):
  1) p99 latency regression: +30% above baseline for 3 consecutive 5m windows AND token-serving CPU > 70% on >50% of nodes in the pool -> P1 alert.
  2) Error budget burn: >25% error budget consumed within 1 hour -> P1 alert.
  3) Cache eviction storms: cache eviction rate > 1e6 keys/min for 10m -> P2 alert.
  4) Hint queue backpressure: prefetch queue length > 2500 for >5m -> P2 alert.

Telemetry and dashboards (required metrics)
- Metrics to instrument (names used by dashboards):
  - runtime.prefetch.hints_applied{route,model,version} (counter)
  - runtime.prefetch.hint_ttl_expirations{route} (counter)
  - runtime.cache.evictions_per_minute{pool} (gauge)
  - runtime.token.cpu_usage_percent{node,pool} (gauge)
  - runtime.slo.p99_latency{route,region} (gauge)
  - runtime.prefetch.synthetics.success_rate (ratio)
- Required dashboards: "Prefetch Safety Overview" (p99 latency, error rate, cache evictions, hint queue length by route), and a per-release widget that overlays hint apply-rate and synthetic success rate.

Operator preflight checklist (before enabling a hint configuration globally)
1) Synthetic harness: run 1000 synthetic requests representative of target route and confirm prefetch.synthetics.success_rate >= 99.5% and p99 within 10% of baseline.
2) Resource smoke test: enable hints in a canary pool (1–5% of traffic) and monitor CPU, GPU memory, and eviction rate for 30m.
3) Cost model check: projected token-cost delta from prefetch must be < 8% of route baseline over first 24h (billing estimator run required).
4) Schema validation: validate hint payload against hint-schema service (hint-schema/v2) and confirm no deprecated fields.
5) Rollout plan: define a canary->ramp->global plan with metric gates and explicit rollback thresholds.

Runbook: responding to a P1 prefetch safety alert
1) Acknowledge P1 and escalate to runtime oncall and the hint release owner.
2) Immediately pause new hint dispatching at the router level: 
   rwlctl prefetch dispatch pause --route <route> --region <region> --reason "safety-alert"
3) If the alert indicates latency or CPU pressure, move canary traffic to fallback routing policy that disables prefetch and switches to cold-start warmup:
   rwlctl route update --route <route> --fallback-policy disable-prefetch-warmup
4) If cache eviction storm is present, trigger a pruned eviction run to selectively evict oldest hints and increase eviction backoff:
   rwlctl cache prune --pool <pool> --strategy oldest --max-evictions 20000
5) After pause, run targeted synthetic suite and inspect: p99, error rate, eviction rate, and hint-apply ratio. If metrics return to acceptable thresholds for 30 minutes, resume a reduced-capacity canary ramp.
6) Communicate incident summary to stakeholders within 1 hour and post a short update to #runtime-ops and the affected customer leads.

Rollback rules and automation
- Automated rollback triggers (enforced by rollout DSL):
  - p99 latency > 40% above baseline for two consecutive 5m windows -> automatic rollback to previous hint version.
  - Error rate > 0.5% for 10m -> automatic rollback.
  - Synthetic success rate drops below 98% during canary -> rollback.
- Rollback command (manual):
  rwlctl prefetch release rollback --route <route> --version <prev-version> --reason "auto/ops-rollback"

Hint retirement (obsolescence) process
- When a hint schema or model variant is deprecated, follow these steps:
  1) Announcement: create a deprecation RFC and notify stakeholders with a 90-day default window (shorter windows require exec approval).
  2) Monitoring: during the deprecation window, flag usage in the "Hint Inventory" and add to the weekly retirement dashboard.
  3) Automatic pruning: after 60 days, start soft-pruning by adding a runtime header to stop new applies (allowing existing cache entries to expire naturally).
  4) Forced prune: after the full window (default 90 days) the operator may run a forced prune that deletes hint metadata and triggers a distributed eviction.
  5) Post-prune validation: run the synthetic suite and a 2-hour regional canary to confirm no SLO regressions.
- Example retirement timeline (text table):
  | Step | Day offset | Operator action | Notes |
  |------|------------|-----------------|-------|
  | Announcement | 0 | Publish RFC + email + docs | 90-day window starts |
  | Soft-prune start | 60 | Stop new applies via header | existing entries expire by TTL |
  | Forced prune | 90 | Delete hint records + eviction job | Use low-traffic window |
  | Post-validate | 92 | Synthetic + canary | Confirm no regressions |

Schema and compatibility rules
- Schema versions must be explicit and backward compatible for at least two release cycles. Version field example: "hint_schema": "v2".
- New fields must be additive. Removal of fields requires a deprecation cycle.
- The runtime will refuse to apply hints with unknown critical_flag fields unless operator enables experimental mode.

Operator tooling examples
- Validate a hint file locally:
  hint-ctl validate my-hint.json --schema=hint-schema/v2
- Apply to canary only:
  rwlctl prefetch apply --file my-hint.json --target canary --max-rate 50/s
- Pause dispatch globally:
  rwlctl prefetch dispatch pause --all --reason "safety-test"
- Forced prune job (example):
  rwlctl cache prune --pool shared-prefetch --older-than 90d --dry-run false

Safety fences and guardrails (runtime + infra)
- Rate limitter: per-tenant prefetch throttle default 2000 hints/s. Increase requires quota approval.
- Token budget guard: if a route’s prefetch token budget would increase projected token spend by >10% for 24h, throttling triggers.
- Feature flags: all new hint versions must land behind the feature flag: ff:prefetch.v2 and be gated by rollout DSL with auto-rollback policies.

Oncall playbook summary (quick steps)
- P1 alert: pause dispatch -> route fallback -> run synthetic suite -> communicate -> rollback/prune as needed.
- P2 alert: open a ticket, evaluate resource pressures, run selective pruning, schedule follow-up.

Post-incident retrospective template (for hint-related incidents)
- Title, incident window, summary of actions taken, root cause hypothesis, detection timeline (who saw it, how), corrective action list (with owners and due dates), validation steps performed, and any product/customer impact. Attach timeline logs and synthetic reports.

Roadmap and known improvements (next 12 months)
- Automated hint decay: auto-prune hints with zero applies for 30d. (Q2 2027)
- Hint simulation harness: per-release offline simulator to predict eviction pressure and cost impact. (Q3 2027)
- Fine-grained per-tenant cost-shaping controls (self-serve in console). (Q4 2027)
- Schema migration tooling with one-click backfill and rollback for 2-version compatibility. (Q1 2028)

Appendix A: example hint JSON
{
  "hint_id": "route-1234-prefix-v2-202701",
  "hint_schema": "v2",
  "scope": {"route": "chat/standard", "model": "redwood-3b"},
  "ttl_seconds": 86400,
  "apply_rate_limit": 250,
  "safety_flags": ["slo_violation_guard", "rate_limit_guard"]
}

Appendix B: contacts and escalation matrix
- Runtime oncall: #runtime-oncall (PagerDuty: PD runtime, Slack: @runtime-oncall)
- Prefetch product owner: Rina Cho (rina@redwood.ai)
- Customer success escalation: cs-led@redwood.ai
